pacing.reason: indeterminate progress, not a transition: splash._tick_bar is a 70ms GLib timer easing the fill toward a 0.9 CAP it deliberately never passes ('+= (0.9 - self._fraction) * 0.08 + 0.003'), and it stops the timer on reaching it. entries.motion: the splash lifts away on departure (the desktop half is another process)
entries.note: Built 2026-08-10 (Codex under the motion lane, M2-verified). ONLY HALF THE ENTRY IS BUILDABLE HERE and that is stated rather than glossed: G1 says 'splash lifts, desktop settles beneath', but the desktop is ANOTHER PROCESS — splash.py can only lift itself. The splash's exit IS under its own control (session.sh backgrounds it; /tmp/nb-ready or a 30s failsafe calls _finish() -> Gtk.main_quit()), so the departure was animatable: a 32px upward toplevel lift on PAGE with DEPART. THE SAFETY ORDERING IS THE IMPORTANT PART, because this runs during BOOT: the existing 180ms quit deadline is ARMED BEFORE the motion is attempted, and any failure to import or invoke nbmotion quits immediately. So a stalled or broken animation cannot hold the boot behind it — the handover happens on the deadline regardless. _tick_bar (system.boot-session) was left untouched. GATE tools/splash_motion_selftest.py, 9 checks, real GTK widgets, drives _finish(). Red-proved by killing the ARGUMENTS: 2 named FAILs. It also reports Gtk.init_check explicitly, so its own numbers can be trusted or discounted on sight. ⚠ ON-HARDWARE RISK TO WATCH, specific to this one: it animates a TOPLEVEL WINDOW's position, and the splash runs BEFORE the compositor on the software renderer. A moving toplevel is exactly the case that can judder without a compositor. Of everything in this pass, this is the entry I would look at FIRST on a real boot.

entries.note: Implemented 2026-08-10 on the design owner's direction ('apps should have an animation on close like when they open'): the departure retraces the arrival (PAPER-PHYSICS B3). system.app-launch is a calm PAGE fade-in of the content overlay on first map, so close is the SAME overlay fading out over PAGE/DEPART, with the real destroy landing in fade_to's on_done. Once-only flag: a second Esc/Ctrl+W closes immediately; any engine failure falls through to the default close, so a window can never become unclosable. Instant-equivalent under policy-still. The old spec line 'collapses back into the icon' described the grow-card era; that card was retired 2026-08-09, so the honest mirror is the fade.

entries.motion: the selected row's colour eases in place on the theme's feedback rule; it does NOT travel (see note)
entries.note:
AMENDED 2026-08-17 BY OWNER DECISION, recorded so it cannot later read as a gate that was quietly relaxed. The entry used to declare SELECT because Article G2 asks the selection highlight to TRAVEL between rows. It never did travel, and the owner's call is that the SHIPPED DESIGN IS THE COLOUR EASE: selection feedback is FEEDBACK, not SELECT. The reasoning is the design language's own -- friction belongs to commitment, never to moving a selection -- and a travelling highlight custom-drawn over a cell-renderer TreeView is not work to land days before a release. So the entry now declares the motion the app actually performs, at the token that describes it. The band was not widened and the row is not exempt: 90ms is checked against FEEDBACK's 70-100ms.

WHAT IS VERIFIED, AND BY WHAT. tools/transition_pacing_probe.py hands gtk.css to a Gtk.CssProvider and reads the rule back out of GTK'S OWN PARSE, so what is checked is what the toolkit accepted, not what the file says: `treeview.view` carries transition-duration 90ms, with zero parse errors. That is a configured-verified row, never a measured one, because a CSS transition creates no nbmotion run and therefore has no frame trace anywhere in the system. It is red-provable through NB_THEME_CSS: drop `treeview.view` from the selector list and the row fails by name.

THE CSS DECLARATION ALONE IS STILL NOT PROOF OF ANIMATION, and that warning from the original note is kept deliberately. What was added on 2026-08-17 is one measurement that goes further than the declaration: on a REALIZED widget with a frame clock, a state change on a treeview.view node was observed interpolating its background-color rather than cutting (3 distinct intermediate values across ~40-57ms of change, repeated 3x; a Gtk.Button in the very same 90ms rule was the control and behaved identically at 4-5 values). So the rule is live, not inert. It needs a display, so it is evidence recorded here rather than a check in the headless gate.

WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN, precisely: that a per-ROW selection change eases. GTK3 paints TreeView rows through cell renderers against a gtk_style_context_save() context inside the widget's draw, not by a state change on the node the rule matches, and no observation available without hardware separates those two. That is the on-hardware look this entry is still partial for -- not unbuilt work.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE for the G2 travelling highlight: the highlight would have to become a drawn OBJECT rather than a row background -- a custom-drawn rectangle over the TreeView, animated between the outgoing and incoming row rectangles on SELECT, kept correct across scroll, sort, filter and the wide search results, and kept from double-drawing under the cell renderers' own :selected background. That is a real piece of work with real ways to look wrong, and it is a design decision, not a defect: it is not scheduled, and this entry is not a placeholder for it.

entries.motion: a newly mounted volume slides open down the column edge
entries.note: Built 2026-08-10 (motion lane). WHAT THIS ENTRY ACTUALLY DESCRIBES, checked against the code before building: the Finder sidebar has NO show/hide toggle — it is packed unconditionally in the body and there is no menu item or shortcut to collapse it — so 'sidebar reveal' cannot mean a whole-column disclosure. The real, frequent state change on that column is a VOLUME ARRIVING: _poll_devices watches the mount set on a timer and, on any change, called _fill_sidebar, which removes every child and repacks from scratch. Plugging in a USB stick therefore flashed the ENTIRE sidebar to show one new row. Now the arriving mount points are diffed in _poll_devices and only those rows are packed inside a Gtk.Revealer, opened via nbtransitions.reveal after show_all (SLIDE_DOWN, SURFACE_IN) — which is exactly G2's 'slides along the column edge', applied to the state change that exists. WHY ONLY THE NEW ROW: the whole column is rebuilt on ANY mount change, so revealing every row would restage rows nobody touched — an unplug, or a second stick, would animate the lot. That is a worse flash than the one being removed, so 'only the arriving row opens' is pinned behaviourally. FUNCTION IS NEVER GATED ON MOTION: a Revealer that cannot be built degrades to a plain pack, and a reveal that raises forces set_reveal_child(True) — a drive that is plugged in must appear whether or not it animates. Gated by tools/finder_sidebar_reveal_selftest.py (17 checks, behavioural: it stubs _devices() and drives the real poll). Red-proved TWICE against scratch copies via FINDER_MODULE_DIR, and the two proofs fail DIFFERENTLY — dropping the arriving diff leaves the volume un-opened (4 named fails), wrapping every row restages the column (4 different named fails). PARTIAL: on-hardware verification with a real USB stick still owed, and this host has none.

IT CANNOT, and the reason is structural, not effort: nbpicker is a modal Gtk.Dialog TOPLEVEL that builds its OWN overlay and blocks in dlg.run(), while present_card/GrowCard need the CALLING app's overlay plus an anchor rectangle — and no anchor ever reaches the picker, because open_file()/save_file() are handed only the parent window. FOR THE DESIGN OWNER: accept the settle as the picker's motion, or decide the picker should stop being a toplevel dialog (a real rewrite that would make it the same object as every other card in the OS), or retire the 'grows from it' wording. entries.motion: rows travel to their new positions
entries.note: Finding 2026-08-08 (motion lane): there is NO clean generic nbtransitions primitive for this, and building one was the wrong plan. Animating rows to new positions means per-frame position change, which re-layouts a Gtk.Box every frame (PAPER-PHYSICS Article F forbids it). The sanctioned way is the cairo pass-through overlay (nbmotion.Damaged + LayerCache) g2048's tile-slide uses — but that only works where the app DRAWS its rows on a DrawingArea (g2048, illustrator canvas, maps, sequencer lanes). A list of real GTK widgets (Gtk.Box/ListBox rows) would need fragile per-widget snapshot-to-surface, out of scope. So reorder is PER-APP for cairo-drawn surfaces (use nbmotion.Damaged directly), not a shared primitive. The shared toolkit (reveal/replace/highlight/PageSwitcher/GrowCard/present_card/spring/Damaged+LayerCache) is complete for what is cleanly shareable.

entries.motion: momentum, bounded rubber-band, no overshoot past the band
entries.note: Evaluated 2026-08-08 (motion lane) and deliberately NOT built — this entry is a glass idiom that does not fit the paper material, and the evidence is against it. (1) Momentum/coast and rubber-band are buoyant, touch-surface motion; paper has weight and damping (PAPER-PHYSICS §D). It also carries no duration token, unlike every real transition here. (2) There is NO shared ScrolledWindow — 37 app modules each build their own, so there is no one place to add it; adoption would be a 37-app per-app change. (3) Apps that scroll a CANVAS actively DISABLE kinetic scrolling because it fights their interaction: illustrator.py:665 and sequencer.py:4293 both call set_kinetic_scrolling(False) (illustrator's comment: a GtkScrolledWindow installs a capture-phase pan/kinetic that captured its canvas drags). An OS-wide smooth/momentum scroll would REGRESS exactly those apps. The correct behavior is GTK's native scroll; the honest 'no overshoot' is simply not adding a bounce. Left unimplemented as a decision, not a gap.

Zoom interpolates in LOG space and the anchor is re-pinned every frame, so it scales ABOUT THE POINTER rather than lurching; on_done lands EXACTLY on the target so the spring overshoot cannot leave ZOOM_FIT unreachable. While view_moving() the eight lanes blit their cached raster scaled and re-render once on arrival (Article F1). Verified against the real nbmotion.ARRIVE call at sequencer.py:3609, not just the marker comment.

entries.motion: transport state, playhead travel
entries.note: Both tokens met by existing mechanisms; verified by the motion lane 2026-08-08 (no new app code needed). FEEDBACK: the transport lit-state (play/stop/rec/LOOP/METRO/MONITOR) is a CSS class swap on .tbtn.on / .metrobtn.on which change background + border-color — both in Papertone's 90ms feedback transition-property list — so they ease on the theme's slight-spring feedback for free (GtkButtons, no app rule overrides the transition). linear: Sequencer._runner (the 100ms transport tick) sets self.pos from engine.position() (the audio clock) or a free-running monotonic clock, redrawn with NO easing. Per PAPER-PHYSICS §D2 a playhead MUST stay linear — a spring there would be a lie about where the sound actually is — so 'linear' is realised correctly by construction. entries.motion: pan and zoom ease the viewport to its new centre and scale
entries.note: Built 2026-08-10 (Codex under the motion lane, M2-verified). Maps is NOT a widget container — it draws its own cairo vector map — so the motion tweens the RENDERER'S VIEWPORT (cx/cy/scale) via nbmotion.animate on PAGE with ARRIVE, not a Revealer. IT SOLVED THE PERFORMANCE PROBLEM THE RIGHT WAY, which was the real risk in this file: the renderer is expensive (LOD, two-pass roads, labels) and the OS targets SOFTWARE rendering, so a per-frame re-render would have been SLOWER than the instant jump it replaced and the app would feel worse. Instead _draw's `need` test skips _render_surface while _view_moving is true and reuses the CACHED surface under a cairo transform (ratio/dx/dy), re-rendering the true vector map ONCE on landing — the same trick as finder's navigation snapshot. Also correct: queue_draw_area damages only the canvas allocation, never the whole window (F1, and the code says so); a generation counter drops a superseded tween; a prior animation is cancelled before a new one starts; and on_done assigns the exact target centre and scale, so a tween cannot leave the viewport a hair off. GATE tools/maps_motion_selftest.py, 11 checks, and unlike the media suite it is genuinely BEHAVIOURAL — only one text assertion (the marker). Red-proved by killing the ARGUMENTS rather than the call (duration=0, easing=None): 2 named FAILs naming the token and the easing. PARTIAL: on-hardware look still owed.
